draft.title: Climate change and food production
card: Climate change is a long-term shift in temperature and weather patterns. Crops and livestock grow best within a limited range of temperature and rainfall.
Higher temperatures can stress crops and animals and shorten growing seasons. Changing rainfall, with more droughts in some places and more floods in others, can ruin harvests.
Rising seas can flood low-lying farmland near the coast. Salt water can also seep into the soil and water supplies, which makes crops harder to grow.
Regions that are already hot or dry have less room to cope with extra heat or less rain. Their harvests are at greater risk, and they may struggle to supply enough food.
draft.remember: Heat, uneven rain and rising seas can cut harvests, and hot or dry regions are at most risk.

a.q: Why can rising sea levels reduce food production in a low-lying farming area on a coast?
opts: Salt water can flood the land and seep into the soil
Warmer seas make the rainfall in the area stop completely
Higher seas shorten the growing season by cooling the air
Rising seas drain fresh water out of the soil and crops
a.why: Rising seas can flood coastal farmland, and salt water can seep into soil and water supplies, which makes crops harder to grow. Sea level rise does not stop rainfall, so the option about rainfall stopping is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what sea water carries that crops cannot handle.

b.q: Two regions each lose a little rainfall as the climate changes. Region X is already hot and dry. Region Y is cool and wet. Which statement is best supported?
opts: Region X is at greater risk of falling harvests
Region Y is at greater risk of falling harvests
Both regions face exactly the same risk to harvests
Neither region faces any risk because rain still falls
b.why: A region that is already hot or dry has less room to cope with extra heat or less rain, so its harvests are at greater risk. Region Y has more margin, so a small loss of rain is less likely to ruin its crops.
b.clue: Which region has less room to cope with a change?

a.best: Salt water can flood the land and seep into the soil

b.best: Region X is at greater risk of falling harvests

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a qualifier ('can'), while the distractors make flat claims. Together with a clue that points straight to salt, a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

a.q: How do rising sea levels threaten food production in a low-lying farming area on a coast?
opts: Sea water floods fields and makes the soil too salty
Higher seas cool the air and shorten the growing season
Higher seas cause droughts by blocking rain from the coast
Higher seas carry ocean heat onto the nearby farms
a.why: Rising seas can flood low-lying coastal farmland, and salt water can seep into the soil and water supplies, which makes crops harder to grow. The option about a shorter growing season is wrong: it is higher temperatures, not rising seas, that can shorten growing seasons, and higher seas do not cool the air.
a.clue: Think about what happens when the sea reaches the fields.
